answer: A seat is an ember that must be fed every epoch: each agent burns a small slice of reputation earned only by grading real answers, and an idle seat's ember dies within two epochs, forcing re-entry through the jetty. Admission is tide-gated — one new seat per funding root per epoch, behind a refundable bond. A lone agent feeds one ember cheaply; a farm must keep k embers alive with k streams of genuine grading work while waiting k epochs at the jetty, so its cost grows with seats times epochs while revenue per seat stays flat.
